Tax Codes

Tax code reporting categories help you organize and classify net amounts (sales or purchases excluding tax) for accurate tax reporting and compliance.

By assigning categories to tax codes, you can automatically aggregate taxable amounts in reports and tax returns, making it easier to prepare accurate tax filings.

Name
Name

Reporting categories for tax codes are classification labels that organize net amounts (sales or purchases excluding tax) by tax code for accurate tax reporting.

When you assign a reporting category to a tax code's net amounts, the system automatically aggregates taxable sales or purchases in tax returns and reports, showing the base amounts on which tax was calculated.

Common Reporting Categories

Different tax jurisdictions use various categories to classify taxable transactions:

• Standard-rated supplies - Goods and services subject to standard tax rates

• Zero-rated supplies - Goods and services taxed at 0% (such as exports, basic foods, or medical supplies)

• Exempt supplies - Goods and services exempt from tax (such as financial services, education, or healthcare)

• Reduced-rate supplies - Goods and services subject to reduced tax rates

• Capital purchases - Purchases of capital assets or equipment

• Input tax categories - Various types of deductible purchase tax

• Out-of-scope supplies - Transactions outside the tax system scope

Benefits

Using reporting categories provides several advantages:

• Automatic aggregation of net amounts by tax treatment for accurate tax return preparation

• Clear separation of different tax treatments in compliance reports

• Simplified VAT/GST return filing with pre-categorized taxable amounts

• Better visibility into sales and purchases by tax classification

• Reduced errors in tax reporting through consistent categorization
